title: JavaScript this Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict this behavior with callbacks, arrow functions, bind, call, apply, timers, and method borrowing.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: Arrow functions do not have their own `this`, so `user.greet()` does not set `this` to `user` inside the arrow function.
`greetLater` is called as a method, so `this` is `user`; the arrow callback inherits that `this`.
`bind(user)` creates a new function where `this` is fixed to `user`.

options.text: It returns a new function with `this` fixed to `context`
It only works on arrow functions

questions.explanation: `bind()` does not call the function immediately; it returns a new bound function.
`call()` sets `this` to `user` and passes the remaining arguments one by one.

questions.prompt: Which call is correct when the arguments are already in an array?
questions.explanation: `apply()` is designed for calling a function with arguments supplied as an array or array-like value.
`apply()` spreads the array values into individual arguments for the function call.
`call(admin)` runs `user.describe` with `this` set to `admin`, so it reads `admin.name`.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between `call()` and `apply()`?

options.text: `call()` takes arguments one by one; `apply()` takes them as an array
`call()` works only with objects; `apply()` works only with arrays

questions.explanation: Both call immediately with a chosen `this`; the difference is how arguments are supplied.
A bound function keeps its original binding. Rebinding it does not replace the first `this` value.

questions.prompt:
Which option best fixes this context-loss problem?
```js
setTimeout(user.greet, 1000);
```
questions.explanation: The wrapper preserves the method call `user.greet()` for later. Option `c` calls the method immediately instead of passing a callback.

questions.prompt: What happens when you try to change an arrow function's `this` with `call()`?

options.text: The arrow function receives the new `this`
`call()` converts it into a regular function
The arrow function keeps its lexical `this`
JavaScript always throws a syntax error

questions.explanation: Arrow functions do not have their own dynamic `this`, so `call`, `apply`, and `bind` cannot replace it.

questions.prompt: Which modern expression is often clearer than `Math.max.apply(null, numbers)`?
questions.explanation: Spread syntax passes array elements as individual arguments, which is often clearer in modern JavaScript.
`call()` runs the function immediately, so `result` receives the function's return value.

options.text: `bind`, `call`, and `apply` all return bound functions for later
`bind` returns a function; `call` and `apply` call immediately
`call` returns a function; `bind` and `apply` call immediately
`apply` is the only one that can set `this`

questions.explanation: `bind()` returns a new function. `call()` and `apply()` invoke the function immediately.
